research_question: Is low accepted-mechanism identification caused by too few contextual observations, or by miscalibrated causal posterior probabilities?
hypothesis: Increasing independent context-1 interventions from 16 to 64 at unchanged historical training and fixed context-0 evidence will raise exact accepted familiar mechanisms by >=20, and learned contextual relationships will outperform equal-budget controls without excessive false acceptance or miscalibration.
pre_primary_tests: 7/7 PASS on small structural fixtures, without prospective primary seeds
ordering: New independent random worlds per seed; for fit context-1, randomized 4-action blocks reused as nested prefixes for all budgets; fit context-0 112 balanced observations fixed; validation 256 balanced held-out context-action pairs; validation never used for fitting or acceptance
capacity: Fixed 256 contextual two-cause 8-bit truth-table hypotheses. No capacity growth, uniform exact Bayes noise model and learned q-specific context-difference prior from the LR-92AD training episodes.
training_design: Regenerate original LR-92AD 128 history episodes via exact pinned source and training seed; verify original training history and weights hashes; no additional meta-training or tuning.
candidate: LR-92AD learned q-conditioned contextual prior; exact 256-state posterior for each fit budget; unseen q=2 uses uniform independence prior.
acceptance_rule: Accepted iff maximum posterior >=0.90 and fit-only binomial misfit survival p >0.01. Keep unchanged across all budgets and arms; evaluation labels never determine acceptance.
calibration: Five fixed posterior-max-confidence bins [0,.2), [.2,.4), [.4,.6), [.6,.8), [.8,1] with weighted ECE against exact MAP mechanism correctness; mean Brier and false acceptances also reported. Confidence cutoff never modified.
metrics: accepted exact familiar/192, unseen/48 at each budget
false accepted mechanisms familiar and unseen at each budget
ECE and Brier of MAP confidence at each budget
full input/outcome receipts, learned-weight cold restore and cost per budget
